html:
The last imperial dynasty of China, founded by the Manchus, which ruled from 1644 to 1912. At its height it roughly doubled the land of the Ming, reaching from Manchuria to Tibet and from Mongolia to Taiwan.

The Manchus were descendants of the Jurchen people of the old Jin dynasty. Their leader Nurhaci united them, and his son proclaimed the Qing in 1636. When rebels took Beijing in 1644, a Ming general let the Manchu armies through the Great Wall, and they took the capital and then all of China. Han men were made to wear the Manchu queue hairstyle as a sign of loyalty.

The High Qing, under three long reigns, was a time of power and wealth:

  • The Kangxi Emperor crushed a revolt in the south and took Taiwan in 1683.
  • The Qianlong Emperor destroyed the Dzungars and annexed Xinjiang.
  • The population roughly doubled in the 18th century, and Europe bought Chinese tea, silk and porcelain through the Canton system.

The 19th century brought collapse from inside and out. Britain beat China in the First Opium War of 1839 to 1842 and forced open its ports. The Taiping Rebellion of 1850 to 1864 killed perhaps 20 million or more. Reformers in the Self-Strengthening Movement built arsenals and ships, but Japan beat China in 1895. The Empress Dowager Cixi held real power for decades. After the Boxer Rebellion of 1900 and late reforms, the Xinhai Revolution of 1911 brought down the dynasty, and the child emperor Puyi abdicated in 1912.
sum: The last imperial dynasty of China, founded by the Manchus, which ruled from 1644 to 1912. At its height it roughly doubled the land of the Ming, reaching from Manchuria to Tibet and from Mongolia to Taiwan.
